headline: BOB'S DISCOUNT FURNITURE RECAST ITS OWN YOUTUBE SERIES WITH FOUR CREATOR COUPLES AND ORGANIC REACH WENT UP 50 PERCENT.  SEASON ONE HAD ALREADY DONE 200 MILLION VIEWS AND 9 MILLION DOLLARS IN SALES
deck: Same show, same format, same brand.  They changed who was in it, from ordinary couples to four creators with a combined audience of 12 million, and the reach moved half again.  The uncomfortable reading is that the casting call was the media buy.
tldr: Bob's Discount Furniture recast its own YouTube series with four creator couples carrying a combined reach of about 12 million and is running 50 percent more organic reach and engagement than season one, which did 200 million views and 9 million dollars in sales.  Put the combined reach of a proposed cast on page one of your next owned-series proposal, next to what that reach would cost as media, and brief casting on audience before you brief the creative.

Amazon studied more than 2 million campaigns on its own platform in June and found roughly 20 percent of a brand's sales value arrives after the standard 7 to 30 day attribution window closes, which hits owned and creator video hardest because those formats create intention rather than catch it.  Re-run one old video campaign and one old search campaign at 90 days instead of 30 and take the gap into your next planning meeting as your own number.

Kick did 773.8 million hours watched in September, up 15.65 percent, and crossed a million average concurrent viewers for the first time, while Twitch fell 5.89 percent to 1.47 billion hours and lost 11 percent of its active channels.  On the EA Sports FC 27 launch Kick carried 43.6 percent of hours watched against Twitch's 48.9, so ask for the platform split before you allocate and put a named share of the budget on Kick.

Billion Dollar Boy's benchmarking arm found one global retailer's creator budget running 69 percent above benchmark across ten markets, worth 4 million dollars over nine months, because local teams negotiate separately and 73 percent of brands still track creator fees in spreadsheets and email.  Build one sheet of every creator fee you paid last year with market and usage rights attached, find the names that appear twice at different prices, and ask your agency in writing to split talent fee from its own margin.

Bannerflow's analysis of 2.33 million creative assets and 155.1 billion impressions across more than 300 advertisers found 78 percent of brands produced video ads this year while only 46 percent served a video impression, and brands like Wyndham and BetMGM are now building in-house teams to mass-produce creative with AI.  Audit how many of your finished video cuts never ran, then require a named media placement in the brief before any new video gets made.

Seven months into OpenAI selling ads inside ChatGPT, one agency watched lead forms arrive while the platform reported zero conversions for two weeks and showed roughly 100 clicks against the 20 it could verify, which is keeping budgets at ten to twenty thousand pounds instead of a hundred thousand.  Stand up your own measurement before testing any unproven platform and agree in writing which number the client gets invoiced against.

YouTube says more than 12 billion of the 35 billion hours of news watched on the platform in 2025 came from connected televisions, which is over a third of the viewing landing on a screen three metres away rather than a phone held at arm's length.  Watch your next finished cut on a real television at living-room volume, fix the type size and dialogue level that fail there, and make those the defaults in your project template.
